extracted.intended_audience: general readers and fans of Phil Hartman / readers interested in comedy performers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for performing sketch comedy, impressions, voice acting, and ensemble supporting work—drawn from Phil Hartman's career and colleagues' commentary. Useful for evaluating or producing sketch/impression performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impression preparation and embodiment
rubrics_metrics.description: He assembled a collection of video footage of the figure he was preparing to impersonate and watched this continually until he 'completely embodied the person'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare impressions by collecting and repeatedly studying source footage; practise until you internalize mannerisms and persona. Paul Ryan credited this method for making Hartman's impressions 'so funny and spot on'. Includes trial-and-error practice and performing in front of audiences and fellow actors to refine the impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in front of audiences / iterative refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: What made [Hartman's impressions] so funny ... was Phil's ability to add that perfect touch that only comes from trial and error and practicing in front of audiences and fellow actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use live performance and rehearsal to iteratively refine timing, delivery, and small details. Treat impression work as a technical craft requiring repetition and audience feedback rather than purely spontaneous mimicry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on subtle, diagnostic mannerisms rather than obvious props
rubrics_metrics.description: Hartman copied the president's 'post-nasal drip' and the 'slight scratchiness' in his voice ... Hartman opted against wearing a larger prosthetic nose ... He instead wore a wig, dyed his eyebrows brighter, and used makeup to highlight his nose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When impersonating a character, prioritize subtle vocal and physical traits that capture the essence without distracting the audience. Avoid over-reliance on large prosthetics that can be distracting; use minimal costuming/makeup to suggest rather than obscure performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a 'utility player' / support the ensemble ('Glue')
rubrics_metrics.description: Nicknamed 'Glue' for his ability to hold the show together and help other cast members ... 'He kind of held the show together. He gave to everybody and demanded very little.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value ensemble skills: listen, react, and create space for others. Strong supporting work — reliable, unselfish performances that elevate the sketch — is a major professional asset. Anti-patterns: high-maintenance or overly competitive behavior that undermines ensemble cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study scripts and disciplined preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: He was disciplined in his performances, studying the scripts beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for performances by studying the script in advance to understand beats, callbacks, and where reactions are needed. Discipline in prep improves timing and consistency in live/sketch environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic timing and delivery via subtle cues
rubrics_metrics.description: He could momentarily fool audiences into thinking he was the straight man, but then he'd cock an eyebrow and give his voice an ironic lilt that delivered a punchline like a fast slider—you barely saw it coming until you started laughing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop control of small facial expressions, vocal inflections, and micro-timing to deliver punchlines unexpectedly. Work on the ability to play straight and then flip with a small, well-timed gesture or tonal shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose roles that reveal character foibles (villains/seedy types can be rich comedic territory)
rubrics_metrics.description: In contrast to his real-life personality ... Hartman often played seedy, vain or unpleasant characters as well as comedic villains. He enjoyed playing such roles because he 'just want[ed] to be funny, and villains tend to be funny because their foibles are all there to see.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When developing characters, consider roles whose flaws and exaggerated traits create obvious comic opportunities. Emphasize observable foibles to generate humor; anti-pattern: bland, featureless characters that lack comedic hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility: develop many distinct characters and vocal identities
rubrics_metrics.description: In his eight seasons with the show Hartman became known for his impressions, and performed as over 70 different characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a wide range of voices, accents, and character types so you can be deployed in many sketches. Versatility increases casting opportunities and usefulness in ensemble shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and low-maintenance collaborative work ethic
rubrics_metrics.description: He was very low-maintenance ... 'He gave to everybody and demanded very little.' Hartman was described as a team player who was never insulted by small roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a cooperative attitude, reliability, and modesty about role size. Being professional and easy to work with fosters long-term collaborations and makes you valuable to productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select projects with strong writing and ensemble chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Hartman signed up [for NewsRadio] after being attracted by the show's writing and use of an ensemble cast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing work, prioritize scripts and teams that offer quality writing and collaborative ensembles; such contexts better showcase supporting players and character actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop characters beyond single sketches (expand backstory / pursue projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: To give Hartman a larger role, they developed the episode 'A Fish Called Selma', which focuses on Troy McClure and expands the character's backstory. Hartman had expressed an interest in making a live action film about Troy McClure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character resonates, consider expanding its backstory and pursuing longer-form projects (episodes, specials, films) to deepen the comedic potential. Guidance includes being proactive about developing and pitching extensions of popular characters.
